key_insight: The paper shows that a previously overlooked electric-quadrupole contribution at finite light momentum produces photon drag, revealing an extrinsic multiband quantum-geometric effect in centrosymmetric crystals.
engineering_relevance: This suggests new routes to enhance nonlinear photovoltaic response in materials with strong multiband mixing, including twisted MoTe$_2$ bilayers, for advanced solar-energy and optoelectronic design.
method: Recast photon drag at leading order in the optical wavevector.
Isolate the interband quadrupole correction to light-matter coupling.
Interpret the term as a multiband metric tensor measuring variation outside the driven two-state subspace.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a theoretical derivation and predicts anomalously large photon drag in strongly admixed multiband systems, but does not describe experimental data.
watch_item: The predicted effect may depend strongly on momentum-space band mixing and finite-wavevector optical conditions, so material-specific validation will be necessary.
paper_title: Extrinsic quantum geometry in the quadrupolar bulk photovoltaic effect
